title: EEG (electroencephalogram)
what: A recording of your brain's electrical activity, using sensors on your head. No current is sent through the sensors. They only listen.
why: For seizures, fainting, episodes of unusual behavior, or to check epilepsy treatment.
duration: usually 20 to 40 minutes; a sleep recording takes longer
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially for seizures and calming medicines. Do not stop them on your own
What your attacks look like and when you had the last one
If flashing lights make you feel unwell

prepare.title: Hair
prepare.text: Wash your hair the day before or that morning. No conditioner, oil, hairspray, or gel. The sensors must sit close to your scalp.

prepare.title: Hairstyle
prepare.text: Take out braids, hair clips, and hair extensions. Do not wear earrings or metal jewelry on your head.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Eat as usual. Hunger can change the recording. It is better to skip strong coffee and energy drinks that day.

prepare.title: Sleep
prepare.text: If you have a sleep EEG or one after a sleepless night, your clinic will tell you how much to sleep the night before.

bring: A towel or a hat. Your hair will be damp from the gel
steps: You sit in a chair or lie down
A soft cap with sensors is put on your head, or the sensors are attached with gel
You are asked to close your eyes and sit quietly
You are asked to open and close your eyes a few times
For about 3 minutes, you breathe deeply and fast
A bright light flashes in front of your eyes
feel: The cap presses a little, and the gel feels cool
Fast breathing can make you dizzy or your fingers tingle. This passes
No current is sent to you. It does not hurt
after: The gel is washed off, and you can go back to your day right away
The report is usually given the same day or within a few days

faq.q: Is an EEG harmful to the brain?
faq.a: No. The sensors only record brain signals. They send nothing into your head. EEGs are done even on babies.

faq.q: Should I stop seizure medicines before an EEG?
faq.a: Not on your own. Stopping suddenly is dangerous. Tell your doctor, and the doctor decides.

faq.q: Can I wash my hair before an EEG?
faq.a: You should. Clean hair with no conditioner or hairspray gives an accurate recording.

reminders.text: EEG tomorrow. Wash your hair without conditioner or oils. Do not do a complicated hairstyle.
